judgements.justification: Every checkable claim behind A's criticisms (undefined fairness, mis-cited and missing related work, uncited known tools) is correct; no criticism rests on a wrong claim.
B's AC gave a spotlight although no B reviewer rated above 7; the tier rests on the AC's own 'very strong contribution' and 'broader community' judgement.
B's Reviewer_8ugy gave a 7 at confidence 3 on generic praise ('very novel', 'very interesting and practical'), and that score is part of the 'uniformly positive' ratings the B AC cited.
The authors' concessions in A (fairness out of scope, Lemma 3.1, importance weighting) answered points A's reviewers had raised; nothing was volunteered to one forum only.
A weighed its flaws as 'major presentation concerns'; B never learned of them, and the points B called minor are covered by weighting differences, not an ignored flaw.
In A the rebuttal raised Reviewer_oRvo (5 to 6) and Reviewer_i7rY to 7; no B score moved.
Only A's reviewers raised the undefined fairness link, the loose Lagrangian extension and the incomplete, mis-cited related work; all are correct and none appear in B.

Both saw that Lemma 3.1 and the importance weighting are standard: B's Reviewer_dTZk listed them as pros while A's Reviewer_i7rY counted them against the paper; B's AC called the shared lower-bound and impact-model issues minor.
Neither AC adopted a single reviewer's position; A summarised all reviewers and B used its own reading.
No score change is attributed to reading other reviews.
The authors answered Reviewer_8ugy's computation question with the choice of epsilon, but that reviewer's score stayed at 7; no score was held down.
B's Reviewer_8ugy posted a thin, late 7 with no reply to the rebuttal, and it counted unchallenged in B's 'uniformly positive' reviews.
A's poster matches its 6, 6, 7, 7 ratings; no AC went below its reviewers.
A's AC voiced presentation concerns, not a positive view overruled by a score threshold.
No below-threshold score was held on a peripheral point.
Both committees read the paper as a theoretical bandit contribution.
A's raised reviewers gave no sign that the technical core was outside their expertise.
A's extra demands concern positioning faults it found, which is R07, not a different bar for the same kind of paper.
B's reviewers praised standard components as pros, but the notes record no checkable wrong claim of novelty or results.
No reviewer kept a below-threshold score after its main concern was answered.
Both committees accepted promised camera-ready fixes; neither refused credit for promises.
Reviewer_oRvo and Reviewer_i7rY edited their scores to match their stated changes.
No off-record extra reviewer.
No clarity verdict split by reviewer expertise; B praised clarity and A's concerns were positioning, not exposition.
Both A raises came with stated reasons.
No AC set aside a silent detractor.
No reviewer in either committee rated above 7.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review stated a case for the higher tier ('very strong contribution', broad interest).

A's reviewers knew the related bandit literature and found missing, mis-grouped and uncited prior work, while B's reviewers took the paper's novelty at face value and read the known components as strengths.
B's 'uniformly positive' matches its ratings; A's summary matches its reviews.
No committee capped the tier on breadth; B called it of broad interest.
A had no misreading low-scoring detractor.
No new experiments were posted to either forum.
No high-confidence expert review was outweighed by low-confidence ones.
Reviewer_oRvo's Appendix B objection was raised in time and the authors answered it.
A's lower ratings match more critical verbal assessments, not a stricter scale.

reasoning: B's spotlight came from its AC's own reading on near-equal, accept-level ratings (R02), with a thin low-confidence 7 counted in the 'uniformly positive' reviews (R03, R12). A's reviewers, who knew the prior literature (R31), found correct positioning faults B never raised (R07) and counted standard components against the paper that B counted as pros (R08); A's rebuttal moved two scores up while B's moved none (R06). The stage 1 candidates (AC enthusiasm, A-only fairness and related-work faults, known components read as strengths, AC setting tier on near-equal scores) are all covered by existing reasons, so none is added.
